entities.summary: The Lex de imperio Vespasiani is an ancient Roman law partially preserved on a bronze tablet. The law was written across two tablets, but only the second survives. The title and preamble of the law are lost. The name by which it is now known is a reconstruction. Lex de imperio Vespasiani is a statute. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.
